Munich chain ladder of paid and incurred claims

Source: R/reserving_one_year_munich.R
munich_chain_ladder.Rd

Projects a paid and an incurred triangle together, so that their ultimates agree: where an origin's paid to incurred ratio is below the average, its paid claims develop faster and its incurred claims slower than the chain ladder's, and the other way round.

Usage

munich_chain_ladder(paid, incurred, sigma = c("log-linear", "Mack"))

Arguments

paid, incurred

Triangles of cumulative paid and incurred claims, as for chain_ladder, with values in the same cells.

sigma

How the chain ladders' \(\sigma\) is found for a period with a single link ratio: "log-linear" or "Mack".

Value

An object of class netsimr_reserve: a list with by_origin, a data frame with each origin's latest paid and incurred claims, their ratio, the Munich chain ladder ultimates of both and their ratio, and the separate chain ladder ultimates; total; the completed triangles paid_full and incurred_full; lambda (paid and incurred), q (the average paid to incurred ratio of each development period) and the two chain ladders.

Details

Following Quarg and Mack (2004), the chain ladder factor of each triangle is corrected by the origin's deviation from the average paid to incurred ratio (\(q_j\), or its inverse for the paid triangle) of the development period: \(\hat f^P_j + \lambda^P \hat\sigma^P_j / \hat\rho^P_j (I_{ij} / P_{ij} - 1 / q_j)\), and likewise for incurred, where \(\lambda\) is the slope of the link ratio residuals on the ratio residuals. The \(\sigma\) of a development period with a single link ratio or ratio is extrapolated log-linearly, as in the ChainLadder package's MunichChainLadder(), whose results the function reproduces.

References

Quarg, G. and Mack, T. (2004). Munich chain ladder. Blatter DGVFM 26(4), 597-630.

See also

chain_ladder.

munich_chain_ladder(quarg_mack_paid, quarg_mack_incurred)
